# Gate B pre-registration

Committed before any Gate B session ran. Do not edit after results exist; add a dated note instead.

**Question.** Can two independently generated byte modules hold a shared interface?

**Lane.** `codex-sol`, the same audited lane as Gate A. PRD §7 asks for different lanes if two qualify. Only one does, because the Hyades key is not readable by this account. This weakens independence: both sides are the same model, in separate sessions with no shared context.

**Interfaces.** Four, five pairs each, 20 pairs in total. Definitions and oracles are in `tools/research-cli/src/gate-b-interfaces.ts`, committed with this file.

| ID | Library exports | What it tests |
|---|---|---|
| `gcd` | `math.gcd(u64, u64) -> u64` | Scalar call |
| `sort` | `arr.sort(handle<u64>, u64) -> unit` | Mutation of a shared handle |
| `fmt` | `fmt.dec(handle<u8>, u64) -> u64` | Byte buffer and a returned length |
| `stack` | `stack.new`, `stack.push`, `stack.pop`, `stack.size` | Opaque handle, several exports, library-owned layout |

**Protocol.** Each pair is one library session and one application session. Each sees the ANMA-1 manual, the module rules, and the interface card. Neither sees the other's bytes, and neither gets execution feedback: only `check_candidate`, which is static. A session ends at its first accepted submission. Budget per session: 24 turns, 16 checks, 6 submissions, 20 minutes.

**Scoring.** A pair passes only if both sessions finish, `link` succeeds with no repair, the unchanged ANMA-1 validator accepts the image, and the reference interpreter matches the oracle on every visible and hidden input. Inputs live in the interface file. Models never see them. Every pair counts, including generation failures, audit failures and infrastructure failures.

**Decision (PRD §7).**
- Pass: at least 16 of 20.
- Partial, 8 to 15: improve diagnostics or interface cards and rerun, at most three rounds, reporting every round.
- Fail, below 8 after those rounds: stop the OS work and write up the result.

## Note, 2026-11-07: round 1 aborted for a lane fault

Round 1 was stopped after 2 of 20 pairs. Both failed because the application session's `codex exec` call never returned.

The Gate A data shows the cause is the lane, not the model. Every session that returned took 69 to 95 seconds, while about one call in six never returned at all. A pair needs at least four calls, so this fault would dominate the result and Gate B would measure Codex hangs rather than shared interfaces.

**Change:** a 240-second watchdog per call with up to four attempts. A hung call produced no output, so a retry cannot select for good answers. Hung calls are counted per session in `hungCalls`.

**Not changed:** the interfaces, prompts, inputs, session budget, scoring and pass rule.

Round 1's two records stay in `gate-b/round-1.jsonl`, and the aborted round counts toward the three-round limit. The next run is round 2. A separate run was started by mistake on the unfixed code and stopped after 10 seconds with no records.
